name: CHAD
lead: Chad sits in the heart of Africa. Sahara Desert dunes meet savannah and green wetlands here. More than 200 peoples live in Chad. Lake Chad in the west once fed millions.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Chad has three bands. The north is Sahara, with sand seas and the volcanic Tibesti mountains. Emi Koussi, a volcano, rises 3,445 m there.
The middle is Sahel, dry grassland for herders. In the south, summer rains turn the plains green. Lake Chad has shrunk to about 10% of its 1963 size.
animals: Zakouma National Park shelters 700 elephants. The herd doubled after rangers stopped poachers (illegal hunters). Hippos wallow in the Chari River. Over 370 bird species fill the air.
Lions, hyenas and rare African wild dogs roam the Sahel. Dorcas gazelles sprint across the dunes. Millions of European birds rest at Lake Chad each winter.
culture: Tubu and Arab nomads (travelling herders) race camels and share three cups of tea. The cups mean life, love and death. Wrestling is the national sport.
Southern music uses the gentle n'goni, a string instrument, and thundering Sara drums. People wear flowing gandoura robes at markets.
history: Chad was the heartland of the Kanem-Bornu Empire, one of Africa's longest-lasting kingdoms. It ruled for nearly 1,000 years. Traders carried salt, ivory and cloth across the Sahara to Egypt.
France took control of the region in the early 1900s. Chad became independent in 1960. Decades of civil conflict followed. Oil was found in 2003, bringing new roads and new tensions.
wows: Lake Chad has shrunk 90% since 1963, from 25,000 km² to about 1,500 km².
Emi Koussi is the Sahara's biggest volcano, wider than Greater London, England's capital region.
Chad is one of the countries furthest from any ocean.
Rock art on the Ennedi Plateau shows crocodiles in dry desert. The Sahara was once green.
Zakouma's elephant herd doubled in a decade because rangers stopped illegal hunters.
In the dry season, you can wade across the Chari River border with Cameroon.
The oldest known human-relative skull, 7 million years old, was found in Chad in 2001.

myths.myth: Lake Chad is named after the country
myths.fact: The country took its name from the lake. 'Chad' means a large body of water.

myths.myth: Deserts are hot all day and night
myths.fact: Dry air holds little heat. Desert nights can fall close to freezing.
